_source.describes: The Wizard Towers generator: its four axes, and what each die in the stack makes of a floor.
_source.status: Unofficial. Not affiliated with Games Omnivorous.
_source.rationale: The stack of d6s with a d4 balanced on top is FLAIL!'s procedure and is implemented faithfully, which the Third Party Licence permits. The words each face resolves to are original to this project. The top floor reads from its own four-row table because the d4 is a different die, not a shorter d6.
_source.attribution: FLAIL! Tools is an independent production by the flail-tools contributors and is not affiliated with Games Omnivorous. It is published under the Games Omnivorous Third Party Licence.

shapes: A plain round drum of grey stone
A spiral that narrows as it rises
Wider at the top than the bottom
A shell of scaffolding, never finished
Low and broad, more keep than tower
occupants: A wizard who has not gone out in years
An apprentice, alone, out of their depth
A rival who took the place by force
Nobody, and the table is still set
A creature the wizard bound and lost to
Two wizards who are not speaking
A servant keeping it exactly as it was
A wizard slowly becoming something else
Squatters who do not know what they touch
reactions: Asks for help, and means it
Asks for help, and does not
goals: To finish a work begun by somebody else
To undo a mistake that is still spreading
To speak with something long dead
To find an apprentice worth the name
To get back inside their own tower
To keep something from getting out
To prove a rival wrong, publicly
To remember what they came here for
floorTypes: One large thing, and no room for more
topFloorTypes: An observatory, open to the sky
The working study, where it all happens
A sealed room, and the seal is recent
